summary: All nine occurrences checked. Active II release has causer, animal causee and ʕal-target; the Detransitive rush has an initiating subject and b-/ʕal-target. The Detransitive here does not require an affected patient as subject.
The overlooking house at 4/14 is a spatial state with an inanimate subject. Preserve the inherited Detransitive sense and example; do not derive a new sense merely from the house participant.
The child-group to single-boy switch mšalṭi/mšalaṭ is in the same MAC verse and already quoted; both tokens receive a decision, with no duplicate.

Read the permitted ṣlṭ lookup: near-identical II directed-sunlight and release material warrants a variant-split question. Do not merge separate glossary roots on similarity alone. The new Infectum claim is local to šlṭ.
Jan's English is project machine translation, copied only as supplied and not used to establish senses. All interpretations were checked against the Turoyo.
Jan adds figurative social and doctrinal domains to the existing broad Detransitive dominance/rushing gloss. Participant type alone does not justify another numbered sense.
Mšalṭo is a feminine predicative state; mšaləṭ is provisionally Detransitive Preterit in an onset context. Their meanings do not require an external causer.
The round-1 active gloss clarification and active engagement sense 2 are retained as context; neither is re-proposed. Jan does not resolve the šlṭ/ṣlṭ variant question.
Should šlṭ and ṣlṭ be cross-referenced or consolidated as variants? Compare the eye/sun constructions and the II forms; no root merge is performed here.
Confirm the causee reading of fronted tre fərṭaʕne with resumptive -ne in 97/20. The preceding command 97/19 supports that reading.
The inherited Detransitive gloss combines dominance, rising and rushing. Is a future internal division warranted? Preserve its numbering until more contrasts are supplied.
Obtain the complete 64/33 context before deciding whether its directed-eye construction needs a separate active sense; the excerpt alone does not settle it.
Confirm mšaləṭ in /1643 as finite Detransitive Preterit versus a predicative state, and the aspectual contrast with mšalṭo in /1642.
Does the inherited broad Detransitive gloss cover social domination and aggressive onset productively? No split is proposed from these participant changes alone.
